_note: Hand-written. No generation, no LLM. Every line here was typed by a person and is shipped as reviewed content (SPECS §9). Trait tags in brackets are display-only until traits exist: the rules layer ignores them. Tiles are overworld coordinates, towns are laid out on the map at their real size rather than entered through a transition. Some lines are gated on a named world condition, the rules layer decides what the name means, so no line reads the world directly.

facts.muster:pay_fraud: Quartermaster Odile at the Muster signs for soldiers who are dead or never existed, and keeps the difference.
facts.kettle:ford: A ford crosses the Kettle downstream of the bridge, shallow only in dry weeks.
facts.wide_acres:unwatched_stall: There is a market stall in Saltmarch that nobody stands near, the marsh town is off the road and keeps no watch worth the name.
facts.acres:land_grants: The land grants for the Wide Acres, naming each village cleared to make them. One of the names is the one you grew up in.
facts.cairnwell:tiered_law: The working record of how the tiered law is administered: three columns, and the third is calculated from the first two.
facts.cinderworks:ledger: The Cinderworks ledger of what the furnaces cost in men, kept in the king's own hand, with the price set against the output.
facts.bank:debts: The bank's book of what the crown owes and to whom. Nearly all of it is owed to one creditor.
facts.muster:signed_orders: The orders to clear the villages, signed. The men who carried them out are named underneath.
facts.cinderworks:death_toll: The Cinderworks has killed somewhere near four hundred men in eleven years. Arthur was sent the count every year and kept sending for more stone.
facts.acres:razed_villages: The Wide Acres estates stand on the ground of villages that were cleared to make them. The grants name every one, and Brindle is on the list.
facts.brindle:the_ground: The farmland north of Brindle is Brindle, the same soil, ploughed over. Old Pell worked it before the burning and works it still.
facts.muster:how_the_king_fights: Arthur trained with his own guard and has never changed his opening. He leads with the shield and counters left, and his officers have drilled against it for years.
facts.thornwood:kell: A deserter called Kell is living rough in the Thornwood, east of Harrowgate, by a fire he keeps too small to see from the road.
facts.brindle:that_night: What happened at Brindle: the order was to clear it, the village did not move, and the men who carried it out were told afterwards that it had resisted.
facts.saltmarch:what_leaves: Steel, grain and coin leave the region by sea, on the crown's order and under nobody's seal. Til has the manifests he was told to lose.
facts.law:the_effects: What the tiered law does, case by case: the same offence, three sentences, sorted by what the accused owns and where they were born.
facts.bank:leveraged: The whole industrial project is borrowed, and nearly all of it is owed to one creditor. Arthur's certainty was a bet.
facts.castle:hesper: Nothing goes into Blackcairn without Hesper's mark. She is the door, and she has no deputy.
facts.church:ledgers: The church's own ledgers, which show what Hesper took and from whom. Anselm keeps them because somebody has to.
facts.castle:the_way_in: How a stranger is admitted to Blackcairn: a name on a supply roll, countersigned, and a face that matches it.
facts.king:his_argument: Arthur's case, in his own words: poverty is the enemy, industry is the only thing that has ever ended it, industry needs land, and the villages that would not move were choosing poverty for their grandchildren. He signed the orders himself and will produce them on request.
facts.blackcairn:the_escort: The escort at the gate is not a fixed number. It is whatever the Muster can still spare, and it has been falling for a year.

maddox.name: Maddox
maddox.greeting: You look like you walked here. Nobody walks here.

options.reply: Depends on the hour. The Reeve says the crown, the crown says the Reeve. Ask Tovin, he'll apologise about it.

options.text: The law here, who does it fall on?
options.reply: Tovin. Office by the square, door's always open, which tells you how much anyone wants to go in.
Fewer than they did. Ask Ossa. She patches the ones who stop going back.
Soldiers. They used to be fed, now they're buying, and there's the same grain as there was.
There's a man drinks here who won't give a name and won't sit with his back to the door. Deserter, or worse.

options.text: There's a man living in the Thornwood, isn't there?
options.reply: Kell. Two winters out there. Ossa goes east with a full bag twice a month and comes back with an empty one.

alt_greetings.text: Bread's up again. Third time this month, and nobody can tell me why.

tovin.name: Tovin the Reeve
tovin.greeting: Registrations inside. Complaints inside. The queue is the same queue.

options.text: How is the law applied here?
options.reply: By tiers. What you owe follows what you have and where your father was born. Somebody has to apply it.

options.text: And you think it is defensible?
options.reply: No. It is written, which is a different thing from defensible.

options.text: Does your office cover the Muster?
options.reply: It should. The Muster judges the Muster, which comes to the same as nobody judging it.

alt_greetings.text: If you've come about the grain levy, so has everyone. The answer is the same.

bell.name: Bell
bell.greeting: Don't lean on that. Ink's wet and the Reeve counts sheets.

options.reply: Three columns. What you own, where you're from, what you owe. The third is worked out from the first two.

options.text: Do you ever copy something you shouldn't have seen?
options.reply: I copy slowly sometimes. Fourteen lines an hour instead of forty.

options.text: Do army papers pass your desk?
options.reply: Not the real ones. What arrives is already clean, and clean paper out of a dirty camp is a thing you notice.

ossa.name: Ossa
ossa.greeting: Sit if you're bleeding. Stand if you're not. You're in my light.

options.text: They say you treat men who have run.
options.reply: I treat whoever bleeds. Papers come after the arm is set, or not at all.

options.text: Then why are so many of them running?
options.reply: Not the fighting. The pay. There's a quartermaster at the Muster, Odile, signing for men who are dead. What reaches the living is nothing.

options.text: Is there one of them you remember?
options.reply: Kell. Thornwood, east of here, small fire. Go loud. If you come up quiet on him he runs.

alt_greetings.text: I saw what you did. Sit if you're bleeding, I said I never ask, and I meant it. But you'll get no more than that from me.

garrick.name: Garrick
garrick.greeting: Mind the wheel. Cheaper than boots, slower than rumour.

options.text: Is the bridge the only way over the Kettle?
options.reply: No. Ford downstream, half a day. Shallow in a dry week. Nobody counts who uses it.
I delivered. Now I deliver less and I'm paid later. Ask yourself who keeps the difference.

options.text: What travels the road besides you?
options.reply: Soldiers, going the wrong way. And people who listen, which is worse.

wren.name: Wren
wren.greeting: Mind your feet. Half of what's under the ash is worth something. The other half cuts.

options.reply: Nobody lives in Brindle. The crows came after the fire and so did everyone else.

options.text: You must know where nobody's looking.
options.reply: That's the only thing I know worth coin. Saltmarch, north edge. A stall nobody stands at, week to week. It's off the road, so nothing that happens there travels.

options.text: What do you sell, and to who?
options.reply: Scrap, to the Forges. They buy metal and ask nothing. That's two coppers a pound and no questions.

halgrave.name: Foreman Halgrave
halgrave.greeting: Mind the slag, it stays hot a day. Third largest works in the kingdom. Only one still making its numbers.

alt_greetings.text: Halgrave puts himself between you and the furnaces, and does not pretend it is anything else.

options.text: What is it you make here?
options.reply: Steel. Rail, plate, tools, and every nail between here and the sea. Before the works this valley buried a child in four every winter. Now it buries one in forty.
Three hundred and eighty-one, in eleven years. I send the figure up every spring. I have never rounded it down. Arthur reads them and sends for more stone.

options.text: You keep a record of that.
options.reply: Of course. The crown requires it. If a thing costs three hundred and eighty-one men somebody had better be able to say so. It's in the office.

sena.name: Sena
sena.greeting: You're not from the works. Nobody from the works stands looking at it.

alt_greetings.text: Sena looks at your hands rather than your face, and keeps her own where you can see them.

options.reply: Furnace four, six years ago. Eleven days' pay and a paper saying the fault was mine.
He'll say three eighty-one. He's not lying, he's counting what he's allowed to count. Men carried out of the infirmary don't go in the book.
They would. What was missing was a number. Nobody walks off a shift for a feeling. A week.

ivo.name: Doctor Ivo Marsh
ivo.greeting: If you're bleeding, sit. If it's about somebody dead, ask me. Don't go through the files.

alt_greetings.text: Marsh goes on writing, and does not look up until you have gone.

options.reply: I sign what I'm given. Crush, burn, fall, fever. Four words and a date.
Honest and wrong. He counts what dies at the furnace. I count what dies of it. Lungs, mostly, eighteen months later, at home.
Because if I go they find a man who keeps no count of his own. That is the whole of my defence and I know what it is worth.

cadan.name: Lord Cadan Vale
cadan.greeting: You are standing on the best barley ground in the kingdom and you have not looked down once.

alt_greetings.text: Vale watches you the way a man watches weather he has already decided about.

options.text: How far do the Acres run?
options.reply: Kettle to the ridge. Four thousand acres, one rent roll. There were nine villages and nine answers to everything.
Nine. Named in the grants, with the date each was cleared. My father took the grant. I took the debt. Barley feeds more people than sentiment.

nessa.name: Nessa Vale
nessa.greeting: My father is expensive to interrupt. The paperwork is me and I'm cheaper.

alt_greetings.text: Nessa keeps the ledger closed with one hand while she talks to you.

options.reply: Grants, rents, boundaries, tithes, the lot. He signs it, forgets it, asks me what it said.
Brindle. Ashcote. Wenn. Upper Harrow. Lower Harrow. Four more. He calls that list an administrative detail.

pell.name: Old Pell
pell.greeting: Mind the furrow. Looks like ground. Mostly stone. Under the stone it's somebody's doorstep.

alt_greetings.text: Pell goes on with the row he is on and lets you stand there.

options.reply: Brindle. This was the top of it. The green, the well, a house with a crooked gate. I ploughed round that gate three years. Still Brindle.
Good people. Slow to lend, quick to give. There were children. Nobody ever said what became of them.

options.text: They could keep the harvest in the barn.
options.reply: They could. Talked about it six years. Never had a reason they could say out loud. Nine villages on paper is a reason. I'll go round tonight.

ryse.name: Commander Ryse
ryse.greeting: You walk into a camp like a man nobody has ever stopped in one. Enjoy that.

alt_greetings.text: Ryse does not turn round. He has already had you described to him.

options.reply: I did. A list and a season. I finished inside both. If you want a man wringing his hands, wrong camp.
Eleven years. Shield forward. Counters left. Always. He learned it at nineteen and nobody has been allowed to beat it out of him.

odile.name: Quartermaster Odile
odile.greeting: Requisitions left. Complaints anywhere. I don't read them.

alt_greetings.text: Odile closes the book before you are near enough to see the page.

options.reply: Exactly as long as the men I am told to feed. If some are a month dead, that is a question for whoever signs above this tent.

options.text: What is Arthur like in a fight?
options.reply: Predictable, and free, because it costs nothing to say. Shield forward, counter left. The guard drilled against him eleven years.

options.text: I know what you are doing.
options.reply: Then name a price. There are quotas, and you are saying it out loud in a tent with thin walls.

kell.name: Kell
kell.greeting: Don't do that again. Don't come up on a man out here quiet.

alt_greetings.text: Kell has his back to a tree and his hand where you cannot see it.

options.text: How long have you been out here?
options.reply: Two winters. Fire, water, and nobody handing out loads. Better than the camp was.
Nineteen. We were told it resisted. It had not. It stood still. That is a different thing and the difference came too late.
Eleven by name. More I don't know. They won't come in for a pardon. They've seen what a pardon is. Somebody who already knows and didn't spit, maybe.

til.name: Harbourmaster Til
til.greeting: Tide went out an hour ago. Anything else, say it quiet and say it once.

alt_greetings.text: Til finds something on the far side of the quay that needs him.

options.reply: Less than there was. More than the book says.

options.text: What leaves, and on whose order?
options.reply: Steel west. Grain west. Coin west. Every month, crown order, nobody's seal. The manifests were to be lost. Copies were.

options.text: A convoy could go the wrong way.
options.reply: Twice already. Both times it was weather. Weather can be arranged.

mira.name: Mira Sand
mira.greeting: Sit or don't. If you're here to tell me the law is the law, I've had that one and I lost it politely.

alt_greetings.text: Mira closes the file she was reading and waits for you to leave.

options.reply: I represent people who can't pay to be represented, under a law that decides what they owe by what they have.
Three men, one wall, one night. Landowner: eleven shillings. Tradesman: four months. Born in a cleared village: seven years. I have four hundred of these.

corvin.name: Corvin Ash
corvin.greeting: You have the look of a man who wants something explained. That's what a bank is for. It isn't free.

alt_greetings.text: Ash has his clerk tell you the house is not receiving.

options.reply: It lends to the crown. The crown builds. Everyone calls that a partnership until a payment runs late.

options.text: How much of it is borrowed?
options.reply: Nearly all of it, and nearly all of that is this house. He did not build the works with money. He built them with confidence, which is a stranger instrument.

peyre.name: Archivist Peyre
peyre.greeting: Quietly, please. Not for the records. Forty years and I've got used to it.

alt_greetings.text: Peyre goes back to his shelving and does not offer you a chair.

options.reply: Everything ever signed. Grants, debts, sentences, requisitions. An archive isn't where a thing is hidden.
Shelf eleven, second copy. Villages listed by name because the surveyor was paid by the name. Nine of them.
Shelf eleven also, which I have always taken for somebody's joke. One creditor, near enough. Not read aloud here in six years.

options.text: Does the church file returns here?
options.reply: Every house files, audited, annually. Theirs balance. They have balanced for nine years.

anselm.name: Brother Anselm
anselm.greeting: The steward isn't seeing anyone. I say that eleven times a day and it's true about ten.

alt_greetings.text: Anselm says the steward is not seeing anyone, and this time does not soften it.

options.reply: She does, then I write it down, then people are cross with me. Hesper is the door into Blackcairn. Not a door. There's nobody behind her.
Because otherwise nobody can check. They show what she has taken and from whom, over nine years.

options.text: What is actually written on the roll?
options.reply: A name, a trade, a quantity, and her mark beside it. I write the first three.

hesper.name: Hesper
hesper.greeting: Four minutes, and you weren't announced. Let's find out which of us is wasting them.

alt_greetings.text: Hesper does not look up from the roll she is marking.

options.text: How does a stranger get into Blackcairn?
options.reply: Supply roll, countersigned by me, a face the gate can match to the name. That's all of it. It isn't negotiable.
Something wanted, or something feared. Neither is often in the room.

aurel.name: Lord Aurel Greyhold
aurel.greeting: I am told you have been asking about the tiers. Ask me. I would rather it came from a man who administers them than from one who merely resents them.

alt_greetings.text: Greyhold decides, visibly, that this is not the morning for it.

options.reply: Every sentence above four months in this region carries my hand. The arguments for it are better made by its enforcers than by its authors.
Nobody has ever put it as though it were available. There is a household, and forty years of signatures. The next one will not be signed.

arthur.name: Arthur
arthur.greeting: You came all this way and you have not drawn anything. Say what you came to say.

alt_greetings.text: Arthur looks at you a long moment and decides he will hear it anyway.

options.reply: Nothing was burned. An order was signed to clear nine villages. Tired, frightened men did the rest. That is a correction, not a defence.
Poverty. Not the crown, not the works. A man on four acres has a short life and buries half his children, and the people who write songs about that life have never lived it.
It could have stopped. The cost of stopping falls on people not yet born, who cannot be asked. The ones who were there refused, and it went on.

options.text: Mine was one of the nine.
options.reply: I know. Not which. Here is what you will hate: they were happy, and poor, and dead at forty. All three at once.
No. It is a trade, and you are entitled to decide the first part mattered more. I decided it did not. One of us is wrong and neither of us can prove it.

options.text: You keep records of all of it.
options.reply: Every page. The dead at the works, the grants with the village names, the orders with my hand at the bottom. A man who hides the cost suspects it was not worth paying.

dray.name: Captain Dray
dray.greeting: Stop there. Close enough for whatever this is.

alt_greetings.text: Dray moves to put himself between you and the gate, without hurrying.

options.reply: As many as the Muster sends. Fewer than last month. The post is meant to hold forty.

options.text: Would they follow you against him?
options.reply: No. Be glad. I have seen a kingdom find that out about itself. It was not better after.

_strangers_note: Generic types, not cast. §6's roster is twenty-five named people and these are not among them: a stranger has a trade, a line set shared by everyone of that trade, and no name. They exist so the world can react to you through somebody who has never met you, which is the whole point of a rumour arriving before you do. Placements are instances; the lines belong to the type.

trader.name: A trader
trader.greeting: Cloth, salt, lamp oil. Coin first, and no, I don't do favours.

alt_greetings.text: No. Whatever it is, no. I've heard about you and I'd rather keep what I've got.

options.reply: Whatever you can pay for. Sit a while, I'll find something you need.
Word came up the road ahead of you, and it was specific.
Busy enough. The counting house keeps the hours and the rest of us keep to them.

guard.name: A bridge guard
guard.greeting: Road's open. Keep it that way and we'll not have a conversation.

alt_greetings.text: You again. Cross, and keep your hands where I can see them.

options.text: Who pays you to stand here?
options.reply: The crown pays for the bridge. The bridge pays for the post. Ask again in a month about either.
A ford downstream. Shallow in a dry week, and nobody counts who crosses. That was not said.
Soldiers, going the wrong way. That is all that will be said about soldiers.

watchman.name: A watchman
watchman.greeting: Works property. Look all you like, touch nothing, and we stay friends.

alt_greetings.text: I know you. Stand where I can see you and keep your hands out.

options.reply: Long enough. The job is to stand here and notice things, and lately there has been a great deal to notice.

options.text: Who told you to watch this?
options.reply: Somebody who signs for it. That is as far up as anyone here has been told.

_dispositions_note: How anybody opens a conversation when they have an opinion of you, used when that person has not been written a line of their own for that band. Narration rather than speech, deliberately: a shared line in nobody's voice sounds flat coming out of a named character, but a shared line about a stance works for everyone. %s is the speaker's name. This is what makes reaction the default rather than something each line has to opt into, before it existed, four of the five named cast chatted normally to a player the whole town had turned on.

dispositions.hated: %s turns away before you can get a word out.
dispositions.wary: %s watches you a moment longer than is comfortable, and waits.
dispositions.welcome: %s is glad to see you, and does not trouble to hide it.
